answer: The wharf multiplier is published, charged in grove, and juniper lists each payment. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The admission burn is multiplied by 11 for every participant already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 4823 identities would post 1647 proofs and burn roughly 13 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
